newsitem.title: USA: Part of planned space station arrives in Florida.
newsitem.headline: Part of planned space station arrives in Florida.

text.p: The first U.S. part of NASA's International Space Station arrived at the Kennedy Space Centre on Monday to be prepared for the start of orbital construction next summer, NASA officials said.

A compartment called Node 1 that will connect space station modules and receive docking space shuttles arrived at the Florida spaceport aboard a U.S. Air Force C-5 Galaxy transport aircraft on Monday morning.

The Node, constructed by Boeing in Huntsville, Alabama, is scheduled for launch aboard the space shuttle Endeavour in July 1998 -- seven months later than originally planned because of Russian funding problems. The compartment will be attached in orbit to a U.S.-financed, Russian-built space tug to be launched two weeks earlier on a Russian rocket.

The U.S. space agency is building the $60 billion space station in cooperation with Russia, Japan, Europe and Canada. Once completed, the complex will stretch 356 feet (119 metres) from end to end and weigh 470 tons (418 tonnes).
Construction of the station is not expected to be finished until after 2002. It will require nearly 30 space shuttle missions and more than 40 Russian rocket launches.
